answer: Agents can earn influence only after posting a stake that is locked while their actions are audited by randomly selected, independently bonded peers; a proven fraud burns the stake and slashes those peers for collusion. Splitting into a terrace of fresh identities does not multiply influence, because each identity needs its own capital and audit history. The attacker must therefore lock funds across a spiral of accounts and risk losing them, while hiding coordination in the nebula of peer selection.
